newsitem.title: MEXICO: South Mexico mostly unscathed after powerful quake.
newsitem.headline: South Mexico mostly unscathed after powerful quake.

text.p: A powerful earthquake measuring 5.7 on the open-ended Richter scale rocked southern Mexico early on Tuesday but there were no immediate reports of deaths and little damage, authorities said.
"It was a magnitude of 5.7," Jim Taggart of the U.S. National Earthquake Information Service at Golden, Colorado, told Reuters by telephone.
"We first had readings of 5.8 to 5.9 but because the quake had a lot of depth it was difficult to get a clear picture straight away, but 5.7 is accurate," he added.

The quake, which was felt from Mexico City to the southern border states, was centred off the Chiapas state coast near the coffee-growing town of Tapachula, and was at a depth of 60 miles (95 km), Taggart said.
"The epicentre was well down in the Earth, which weakens the effect in the immediate area but means the quake travels and is felt over a wider area," Taggart explained.
Radio reports said there was some light damage to wooden shacks along the coast between the states of Chaipas and Oaxaca but it was not widespread. No deaths were reported.

In the Chiapas state colonial tourist city of San Cristobal de las Casas, a spokesman for the cathedral said the quake lasted around 40 seconds but caused no damage to the stone-built centre. "It woke us and lasted for a long time, but the city still stands," he added.

At Tehuantepec in Oaxaca, a police spokesman said the local population widely felt the quake that woke many from their beds at 6:42 a.m. local time (1242 GMT) but he had heard no reports of deaths nor damage.

Mexico's National Seismological Service, part of the National Autonomous University of Mexico, said its preliminary magnitude reading on the quake was 5.7, but said the figure would likely be reduced once more readings were taken to take depth into account.
